name: lock-detector
description: window-comparator lock detector: assert/deassert acceptance over the full PVT grid, and the comparator window's edges over a phase-error ladder at the PVT extremes
claim: #11 -> DR-002 Decision 4 (design input, not a spec line) -- does the window-comparator lock detector assert once the phase error has stayed inside its window, refuse to assert on a large static phase error or on a frequency error, and deassert when the loop is deliberately perturbed out of lock -- at every PVT corner? And where are the EDGES of that window, measured rather than inferred? DR-002 Decision 4 puts a digital lock output in v1 scope as a passive monitor (no band-search or calibration FSM), and names #12's closed-loop testbench as the consumer of the signal.
methodology: Stimulus models the tri-state PFD's UP/DN pair: with the reference edge leading the feedback edge by tau, UP is high for tau + t_reset and DN for t_reset (ktrst = 1 ns), both falling on the reset path, so the DUT's input XOR sees exactly tau and the common reset overlap cancels.

Five independent DUT copies share each transient: swept phase error (this manifest's 'terr' sweep axis); deep in lock (tau = 0); deep out of lock (static tau = Tref/4); frequency error (feedback train 25% slow, so the error pulse beats through every width from 0 to Tref); and a copy that starts in lock and is kicked to a sustained tau = kterrbig at t = ktpert.
Every integrating node is forced to 0 V at t=0 (.ic in the fragment), so each copy starts NOT locked and has to earn the assertion inside the run rather than inherit it from the DC operating point.

The XC (deep-out-of-lock) and XD (frequency-error) assert-time measurements are marked 'optional' with 'max_measured_points: 0' checks: they must NEVER fire, and per sim/harness's expected-.measure-failure handling an absent optional result is recorded as not-measured data rather than failing the point and discarding the point's other, successful measurements -- the exact failure mode this campaign's pre-harness runner (run_deck_soft) worked around by treating 'did the transient finish' rather than 'was the log clean' as the completion test.
The XB (deep-in-lock) assert and XE (perturbation) deassert measurements are marked 'optional' with 'min_measured_points' checks equal to the full point count: they must ALWAYS fire.

Per-point pass/fail verdict (testbench/derive.py 'lock_pass') replicates the pre-harness runner's acceptance formula verbatim: deep-in-lock asserted and stayed HIGH (lb_lvl), deep-out-of-lock and frequency-error stayed LOW (lc_lvl/ld_lvl), the swept copy asserted before the perturbation kick and the perturbed copy deasserted after it. 'Before the kick' is tested as assert-time < kick-time rather than as a level averaged over the run-up to the kick, because at the slowest corners the assert transition itself falls inside any such averaging window and would read as CHATTER -- an artefact of the window, not of the flag.

Window-edge table (testbench/derive.py 'derive_tables', table 'window_edges'): for each window-ladder corner, the largest phase error that still left the swept copy asserted and the smallest that did not -- only computed for corners the run actually stepped 3+ distinct phase errors at, matching the pre-harness reduction exactly.

Verdicts are taken from levels averaged over the last 10% of the run and classified HIGH (>90% of the rail) / LOW (<10%) / CHATTER (anything between) -- that distinction is the whole point of putting hysteresis (the Schmitt readout) in the DUT.
Simulator settings: tran 200p 3.40u, reltol 1e-3, abstol 1e-10, vntol 1e-5, chgtol 1e-13.

Limitation -- low end of the reference range. The assert time is set by a weak pull-up charging a MOS capacitor, i.e. an absolute time, not a count of reference cycles. Reliable deassert requires that hold-off to be much longer than one reference period; at the 25 MHz characterised here that is tens of reference cycles, but extrapolating the same hold-off to the 1 MHz bottom of the draft reference range leaves only of order one reference period, where the flag would be expected to chatter. That extrapolation is a hand argument, not a measured result -- this record makes no claim at 1 MHz.
Limitation -- absolute window. The comparator window t_win is an inverter-chain delay, so it is an absolute time and its ratio to the reference period changes across the reference range.

Limitation -- schematic-level. No extracted parasitics; the integrating node is high-impedance and its post-layout capacitance and leakage will move both the assert time and the window. #18 must re-take this.
This record supersedes 20260731-162119-0a12e6c (same claim, same 95-point corner matrix, run through the sim/lib/simenv.sh shim rather than sim/harness) as a tooling migration.

grid.description: full 45-point PVT grid at a fixed phase error (4 ns) comfortably outside the nominal ~1.2 ns window, so the grid point is an unambiguous out-of-window case at every corner
phase-error ladder at the nominal corner
phase-error ladder at the hot/low-supply extreme of the slow and fast MOS bundles
phase-error ladder at the cold/high-supply extreme of the slow and fast MOS bundles
